correctness.rationale: Every even integer with \(\Omega(n)\le3\) is a power of \(2\), one of \(2p,4p,2p^2\), or a squarefree \(2pq\). Substitution into \(\sigma(n)=4\varphi(n)\) leaves \(p=7\) in the two-support cases and \((p-7)(q-7)=48\) in the three-support case. The latter has only one prime-coordinate factor pair, \((11,19)\). Direct evaluation verifies \(14\) and \(418\), and the packaged checker independently corroborates the classification.

value.rationale: The source paper explicitly isolates the even quotient-four three-support case as the remaining exceptional branch of its low-support program. Total prime-factor multiplicity is a standard independent complexity measure, and \(\Omega(n)\le3\) is its first boundary that reaches the unresolved branch. The theorem closes that boundary globally, explains the uniqueness of the listed example \(418\), and shows that every later even solution must cross to at least four total prime factors.
